text:
infra-bot: :warning: hosted-eu2 GPU pool p95 queueing spiked to 980ms, admission control started rejecting low-priority requests at 1768901234. alert_id=eu2-gpu-queue-1768901234

maya: saw the alert. dashboards show queue depth rising in the last 90s, headroom down to ~6% on the n1 pool.

jonah: is this noisy alerting again or a real capacity event? I see a correlated jump in proxy retries.

priya: looks correlated with a spike in small batch inference jobs from customer-rc. batching histogram shifted to 1-2 tokens, lots of short lived sessions. maybe traffic pattern change after their rollout.

lucas: also seeing increased pod restart counts on a subset of hosts, possible kubelet OOMs? pulling logs now.

maya: runbook check: can we try fallback routing to euw1 for best-effort traffic? we should keep reserved capacity for gold customers in eu2.

jonah: agree. pushing temporary routing tweak now: `curl -X POST https://orchestrator/api/v1/routing/adjust -d '{"from":"hosted-eu2","to":"hosted-euw1","percent":20}'`

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Routing change queued by jonah. job_id=route-4567. estimated propagation 30s.

priya: FYI the autoscaler for that pool didn't trigger new nodes — `scale-controller` logs show 429 from cloud API for create-instance, maybe quota throttle.

lucas: ah — cloud team reported temporary vm-creation limits in eu-west-2 region earlier. that would block adding headroom. can someone check quota console? @maya

maya: on it. opening ticket with cloud support now, but likely 30-60m for quota bump. we need short-term mitigations.

jonah: if cloud quota is the blocker, we should temporarily relax batching to increase concurrency per GPU — trade latency for throughput. suggest lowering max_batch_delay from 12ms -> 4ms for hosted-eu2 pools (config path: `runtime/batching/eu2/*`).

priya: I can roll that change for best-effort models only. will patch canary now and watch p95.

infra-bot: telemetry: after initial routing change and canary batching tweak, p95 dropped to ~420ms at 1768901265. queue depth reduced ~35%.

lucas: still seeing ~2 hosts with kubelet restarts -> digging into dmesg, possible GPU driver race. collecting GPU plugin logs: `journalctl -u nvidia-device-plugin -n 200`

maya: good catch — if host instability persists we should cordon those nodes to avoid noisy neighbours. can we cordon and drain gracefully?

jonah: cordon started on host eu2-gpu-047 and eu2-gpu-051. drain won't evict pods pinned to local SSDs but will stop new allocations.

priya: can confirm canary change applied to 20% traffic, safe so far. will increase to 50% if p95 stays <=500ms for next 2m.

maya: tracking the cost side — increasing concurrency and cross-region routing will shift unit costs. open question: do we prefer temporary cost delta or degraded latency for silver tiers?

lucas: let's prefer preserving gold SLA and accept short-term cost bump for silver. document in incident notes and tag billing-alerts.

infra-bot: incident-note: triage started by maya. tags=[capacity, routing, autoscaler, cloud-quota, billing]. thread_id=1768901234

jonah: next steps: 1) monitoring — keep p95 and queue metrics on a fast refresh dashboard, 2) cloud quota request follow-up, 3) cordon problematic hosts until driver patch applied, 4) evaluate permanent routing policy tweak if customer rollouts consistently spike short jobs.

priya: I ran a quick grep of recent customer rollout IDs; one customer pushed a global canary at 1768901200 that matches traffic spike. alerting: add anomaly detection for sudden shift in token distribution (many 1-5 token requests).

maya: agreed — add that metric to the capacity dashboard and set a 60s window alert.

lucas: local note: collected driver traces and uploaded to s3://redwood-dumps/eu2/driver-trace-176890. attaching to ticket.

jonah: p95 now stable ~360ms, queue depth trending down, routing job completed. setting this thread to monitoring state, will reopen if >500ms again. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident-resolved (monitoring). resolution_summary="routing fallback + batching canary reduced queueing; blocked autoscaling due to cloud quota; cordoned two unstable hosts; followups: quota request, driver patch, new anomaly alert for token-length distribution."
